toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS comma: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have their own subject and verb ('n Woltrui het ... / 'n brood het ...).
toegepas.rede_keurder: Correct AWS 2017 comma; meaning and the protected 'n Woltrui are untouched.

toegepas.voor: Wol en koring en water is
toegepas.rede_vinder: A list of three reads more naturally with a comma than with a repeated 'en'.
toegepas.fout: The repeated 'en' in a three-item list reads clumsily.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A plain list with a comma is the natural form and changes nothing in meaning.

toegepas.rede_vinder: A comma after the long fronted relative clause marks where the subject phrase ends and makes the sentence easier to read.
toegepas.fout: Without a comma the fronted object phrase runs into the main verb ('gebruik noem'), which makes the reader stumble.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The comma marks where the long fronted phrase ends; this is study text, not the glossary definition.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Brei' is the standard Afrikaans verb for knitting; 'strik' in this sense is more regional.
toegepas.fout: 'gestrik' disagrees with the sub-topic's other lesson, which says 'gebrei' for the same jersey; 'brei' is also the standard verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Decided HOU by a person so that the two lessons agree.

toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS comma: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb ('n Meule maal ... / 'n bakker bak ...).

toegepas.na: die koring waarmee alles begin het
toegepas.rede_vinder: The subjectless passive 'waarmee begin is' is wooden; an active form reads naturally and echoes the first block.
toegepas.fout: The subjectless passive 'waarmee begin is' is wooden.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'waarmee alles begin het' is what a fluent writer would say and keeps the same meaning.

toegepas.blok: Waarom party hulpbronne meer werd is
toegepas.voor: 'n Hulpbron wat ver moes kom is hier meer werd as waar dit uitgehaal is
toegepas.na: 'n Hulpbron wat van ver af moes kom, is hier meer werd as daar waar dit uitgehaal is
toegepas.rede_vinder: Adds the comma after the fronted relative clause, uses the idiomatic 'van ver af', and gives the comparison a proper second term ('daar waar').
toegepas.fout: The comparison lacks its second term ('as waar'), 'ver moes kom' is loose, and the fronted relative clause has no comma.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'van ver af', 'as daar waar' and the comma fix real faults without moving the meaning; the protected sentence before it is untouched.

toegepas.rede_vinder: The second clause still belongs to the 'dan' main clause, so it keeps the inverted verb-subject order.
toegepas.fout: After 'Was ..., dan is daar ...' the coordinated consequence keeps straight order, which loosens its link to the condition.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Inverted 'en styg die waarde' keeps both clauses under 'dan', so the rise is clearly a result of the poor harvest.

laat_vaar.blok: Waarde en prys is nie dieselfde nie
laat_vaar.na: as vir iemand wat by 'n kraan staan
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Completes the parallel with 'iemand wat ver geloop het' so the comparison reads smoothly.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'iemand by 'n kraan' already reads naturally; the proposal adds an action and length without a clear gain.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: With 'in die een jaar' just before, the definite article reads more naturally: the harvest of that year.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The indefinite 'n oes reads well as a general condition; the definite article is a lateral move.

vlae.blok: Waarom party hulpbronne meer werd is
vlae.rede: 'Hier' has no clear reference point for the learner (here where it is sold or used?); clarifying it would mean guessing the intended wording, so it is flagged rather than changed.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: 'n Vervaardigde goed is meestal meer werd as die grondstof
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: 'Goed' as a countable singular ('n vervaardigde goed') is unusual in Afrikaans, which normally says 'goedere' or ''n vervaardigde produk'; a person may want to check that this protected wording is what was intended.
